court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: III Additional Family Court, Chennai - O.P.No.2940 of 2007
case_name: Jerry Garman @ Geraldine @ Jayalakshmi vs A.S.Sethuraman
facts_of_case: The wife filed a petition for divorce under Section 10(1)(x) of the Indian Divorce Act. The husband filed an interlocutory application to dismiss the main petition on the ground that the marriage was solemnized as per Hindu rites and customs, hence the original petition was not legally maintainable. The trial court allowed the interlocutory application, which the wife is challenging in this appeal.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu marriage may be solemnized between any two Hindus if the conditions specified in Section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 are fulfilled.
legal_principles.held: it is relevant to extract Section 5 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu convert to Christianity does not need to undergo any expiatory ceremonies before reverting back to Hinduism.
legal_principles.held: His conduct and the circumstance that he was received by his community, were sufficient to establish his reversion to Hinduism

outcome.final_order: The order of the trial court allowing the husband's interlocutory application to dismiss the main petition is set aside.

use_for_drafting: representing clients in family court proceedings
